features.title: Render the product entry page
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can open the app and see an X-META Video entry page instead of a blank screen or generic starter content.
verification: Open the app.
Verify the page shows the X-META Video name.
Verify the page describes AI comic drama, MV, and short-form video creation.
Verify the page does not show unrelated conversation or generic template content.
evidence: Corrected the prior basic shadcn-only treatment by adding `apps/web/src/app/animated-entry-page.tsx`, an animated X-META Video entry page adapted from the UI TripleD Hero Block shadcn/Framer Motion source pattern.

Refactored the one-off animation treatment into `apps/web/src/components/ui/triple-motion.tsx`, a reusable local UI TripleD-inspired component layer for animated background, links, buttons, cards, panels, and expandable info cards.
Added local shadcn/Radix-style `apps/web/src/components/ui/collapsible.tsx` plus `@radix-ui/react-collapsible` so production mode cards have real click-to-expand open/closed state.

Kept `apps/web/src/app/page.tsx` as the app-root route and delegated rendering to the local animated entry page while preserving product-specific AI comic drama, MV, and short-form video creation copy.
Added `framer-motion` because the selected UI TripleD Hero Block pattern uses Framer Motion for reveal, hover, spring, and scroll indicator animation effects.
Kept UI TripleD as copied/adapted local source guidance rather than adding an opaque UI TripleD runtime dependency; local shadcn/ui components remain the component base.

Updated render tests to assert `data-uitripled-source="hero-block"`, `data-animation-runtime="framer-motion"`, `data-uitripled-motion-system="triple-motion"`, animated component markers, and three initially collapsed production cards in addition to the required product copy and generic-content rejection.
`corepack pnpm --filter @xmeta/web test` passed with 2 test files and 5 tests.
`corepack pnpm --filter @xmeta/web typecheck` passed.
`corepack pnpm --filter @xmeta/web build` passed and statically generated `/` and `/icon.svg`.

Browser plugin QA opened `http://localhost:3000` at 1440x900 and 390x844; title was `X-META Video`, required product copy was present, UI TripleD/Framer Motion/triple-motion component markers were present, no generic starter/chat content was present, no console errors or page errors were reported, and there was no horizontal overflow.

Interaction check: the first production mode card changed from `aria-expanded=false` to `aria-expanded=true`, `data-state=open` was present, and the expanded info copy plus `Scenes`, `Dialogue`, and `Characters` tags became visible on desktop and mobile.
Interaction check: `Review production modes` navigated to `#production-modes`; `See canvas direction` navigated to `#canvas-preview`.
Animation check: the scroll indicator changed position during a timed browser probe, confirming live Framer Motion animation was active.
`.\init.ps1` passed after implementation; Vitest ran 2 files with 5 passing tests.
Reflowed the main page with `ui-ux-pro-max` layout priorities while preserving the existing shadcn/UI TripleD style: left hero + actions, right canvas preview, and a separate production modes band.
features.notes: Frontend-only page shell; no backend, auth, or persistence required.

features.title: Add the create-project entry point
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can click a primary Create Project action and see clear project-start choices for comic drama, MV, or short-form video.
verification: Open the main page.
Click Create Project.
Verify project-start choices become visible.
Verify the choices are specific to comic drama, MV, and short-form video.
evidence: Changed the primary homepage action to `Create Project` in `apps/web/src/app/main-page-content.ts`.
Added frontend-only project-start choice content for `AI comic drama`, `MV creation`, and `Short-form video`, each with product-specific descriptions and expected planning output.
Updated `apps/web/src/app/animated-entry-page.tsx` so clicking `Create Project` toggles a `project-start-choices` panel with `aria-expanded` state and `data-project-start-choice` markers.
The create-project panel explicitly states that real project creation, persistence, and workspace routing arrive in Feature 2.
Reused existing local shadcn/ui and `triple-motion` components; no backend, API, auth, routing, persistence, canvas execution, or AI generation behavior was added.
Updated `apps/web/src/app/page.test.tsx` to assert the `Create Project` entry point, initial closed state, and generic-content rejection.
`corepack pnpm --filter @xmeta/web test` passed with 2 test files and 6 tests.
`corepack pnpm --filter @xmeta/web typecheck` passed.
`corepack pnpm --filter @xmeta/web build` passed and statically generated `/` and `/icon.svg`.

Playwright QA against `http://localhost:3000` at 1440x900 and 390x844 confirmed `Create Project` changed from `aria-expanded=false` to `aria-expanded=true`, the three project-start choices became visible, Feature 2 boundary copy was visible, no generic chat/starter content appeared, no console errors or page errors occurred, and no horizontal overflow was detected.
Repositioned the create-project choices into the canvas preview panel during the `ui-ux-pro-max` layout reflow; the primary action remains visible and stable in desktop and mobile open/closed states.
features.notes: This is a UI entry state only; actual project creation belongs to Feature 2.

features.title: Add recent-work entry points
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can find the recent work area and understand where existing projects can be reopened.
verification: Open the main page.
Locate the recent work area.
Verify it shows either project cards or a clear empty state.
Verify the visible action points toward opening or creating project work, not messaging.
evidence: Added static local recent-work entries in `apps/web/src/app/main-page-content.ts` for `Neon alley comic pilot` and `Midnight chorus MV`.

Rendered a `Recent work` section in `apps/web/src/app/animated-entry-page.tsx` with project-style cards, `Open project outline`, `Open production plan`, and a clear `No saved cloud projects yet` empty-state note.
Recent-work actions point to the workspace entry placeholder instead of chat or messaging behavior.
Updated `apps/web/src/app/page.test.tsx` to assert recent-work markers, example project entries, actions, and empty-state copy.
`corepack pnpm --filter @xmeta/web test` passed with 2 files and 10 tests.
Rendered QA at 1440x900 and 390x844 confirmed the recent-work section and actions were visible/reachable with no horizontal overflow or console/page errors.
features.notes: Use static or local placeholder data only until project persistence exists.

features.title: Add the workspace entry path
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can click an Enter Workspace action from the main page and reach a clear creative workspace entry placeholder.
verification: Open the main page.
Click Enter Workspace.
Verify the app shows a workspace entry placeholder or route target.
Verify the copy makes it clear the full workspace shell is a later feature.
evidence: Added `workspaceAction: "Enter Workspace"` and workspace placeholder copy in `apps/web/src/app/main-page-content.ts`.
Added an `Enter Workspace` hero action in `apps/web/src/app/animated-entry-page.tsx` that anchors to `#workspace-entry`.
Rendered `Workspace entry placeholder` with explicit copy that the full workspace shell, saved projects, canvas routing, and execution controls belong to Feature 2 and Feature 3.
Added a UI-only `Create project direction` action from the placeholder that opens the existing frontend-only project choice state without creating persistence or backend calls.
Updated `apps/web/src/app/page.test.tsx` to assert the workspace action, `#workspace-entry` target, placeholder copy, and UI-only boundary label.
Rendered QA confirmed `Enter Workspace` navigated to `#workspace-entry` and the placeholder remained visible on desktop and mobile.
features.notes: Do not implement the full canvas or app shell here; that belongs to Feature 2 and Feature 3.

features.title: Show the creation workflow preview
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can scan the main page and understand the planned flow from brief to script, storyboard, assets, audio, video, and export.
verification: Open the main page.
Verify the workflow preview includes script, storyboard, character or scene assets, audio, video, and export.
Verify the workflow reads as a production pipeline, not a messaging UI.
Verify each workflow item has concise user-facing copy.
evidence: Expanded `canvasNodes` in `apps/web/src/app/main-page-content.ts` into six workflow steps: Script, Storyboard, Character and scene assets, Audio, Video, and Export.
Added workflow icons, labels, and concise user-facing detail copy while keeping the preview marked as `Static orientation only`.

Updated the `Creation workflow preview` panel in `apps/web/src/app/animated-entry-page.tsx` to render the full production pipeline with `data-workflow-preview="production-pipeline"` and `data-workflow-step` markers.
Updated `apps/web/src/app/page.test.tsx` to assert every required workflow step and the static-orientation boundary.
`corepack pnpm --filter @xmeta/web build` passed and statically generated `/`, `/_not-found`, and `/icon.svg`.
Rendered QA confirmed all workflow steps were present and the page did not read as a messaging UI.
features.notes: This is a visual orientation element only; node execution is out of scope.

features.title: Make the main page responsive
features.user_visible_behavior: A user can use the main page on desktop and mobile sizes without clipped text, overlapping controls, or hidden primary actions.
verification: Open the app at a desktop viewport.
Verify all main page sections align without overlap.
Open the app at a mobile viewport.
Verify primary actions, recent work, and workflow preview remain readable and reachable.
evidence: Adjusted the main page layout to include recent work and workspace placeholder sections without hiding the first-viewport primary actions.
Used responsive grids and full-width mobile action buttons so primary actions, recent work, workspace entry, workflow preview, and production modes remain readable and reachable.
Rendered QA at desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844 found no horizontal overflow: document/body scroll width matched client width in both viewports.
Rendered QA confirmed `Create Project`, `Enter Workspace`, `Review production modes`, and `See canvas direction` were in the initial viewport on desktop and mobile.
Rendered QA found no console errors, no page errors, and no missing required section text on either viewport.
`git diff --check` passed with only LF-to-CRLF working-copy warnings.
features.notes: Responsive behavior is part of the main page design definition of done.

features.title: Verify main page accessibility basics
features.user_visible_behavior: A keyboard user can tab through the main page actions in a sensible order and understand each action label.
verification: Open the main page.
Use Tab to move through interactive elements.
Verify focus order follows the visual layout.
Verify each button or link has a clear accessible label.
evidence: Added clear accessible labels for `Create Project`, `Enter Workspace`, `Review production modes`, `See canvas direction`, recent-work actions, and the workspace placeholder create action.
Added `role="region"` with `aria-labelledby` on workflow preview, recent work, and workspace entry sections.
Set non-interactive workflow and recent-work cards to `interactive={false}` so Framer Motion does not add them to the Tab order.
Updated `apps/web/src/components/ui/triple-motion.tsx` so the animated production mode `article` wrapper has `tabIndex={-1}`, leaving the internal expand/collapse button as the keyboard target.
Keyboard QA at 1440x900 and 390x844 confirmed focus order starts with home, hero actions, recent-work actions, workspace placeholder action, then production mode buttons.
Updated `apps/web/src/app/page.test.tsx` to assert accessibility and responsive section markers.
features.notes: Keep this limited to the main page; full app accessibility coverage belongs to later feature work.
